steps.text: This looks like T1037.001 logon script persistence, likely from Atomic Red Team testing—I'm examining the parent process and its relation to the registry value being modified.

arguments.reasoning: Identify the parent process that launched reg.exe.
Get the registry value entity written.
Inspect parent process command line and its other activity (e.g. art.bat creation).
Check which file the cmd.exe parent wrote (likely art.bat).
Confirm the written file is the art.bat logon script payload.

steps.text: Checking for a parent process relation to cmd, but since there's no win_process_create event in the incoming data, cmd must be the root process here. That's sufficient for my analysis.

submission.reasoning: An interactive cmd.exe (proc-23dc9b1636) on workstation5 running as WORKSTATION5\wardog wrote C:\Users\wardog\AppData\Local\Temp\art.bat at 02:46:45. At 02:47:08 it launched reg.exe (proc-55d9f85e37, High integrity), which ran 'REG ADD HKCU\Environment /v UserInitMprLogonScript /d ...\Temp\art.bat'. This sets up logon-script persistence (MITRE T1037.001): the batch file will run every time wardog logs on. The art.bat filename and the Temp location match the Atomic Red Team test for this technique. The evidence chain is complete: the payload was written, then the autostart value was set to point at it.
